goals: Provide clean standalone wearable-lantern functionality for Minecraft Java 26.2 Fabric.
Add a dedicated amount-one Trinkets lantern slot independent of legs/belt and position it immediately left of the vanilla leggings slot while preserving the belt independently on the right.
Render the equipped lantern on the player from the actual resource-aware ItemStack model so generic resource-pack changes propagate without copied vanilla textures.
Support optional dynamic lighting through the current lighting stack without mutating world or server block light.
Allow supported lantern items to be extended through a narrow dedicated item tag without permitting arbitrary items.
scope: Implement a native legs/lantern Trinkets slot assigned to players, with amount one, a dedicated modern GUI sprite, normal Trinkets persistence, synchronization, equip, quick-move, and death/drop behavior, plus a minimal public Trinkets predicate that accepts only membership in the exact trinkets:legs/lantern tag, initially containing minecraft:lantern and minecraft:soul_lantern.

Give the lantern slot an order immediately after the built-in legs/belt order so normal Trinkets layout produces lantern-left, leggings-center, and belt-right whenever both additional slots are assigned.

Use Trinkets' native alternating layout, hover/reveal, quick-move, and group-background behavior for Canary 1; with belt order -1024 and lantern order -1023 both assigned, native positioning yields lantern-left, leggings-center, and belt-right, while belt-absent positioning is recorded for a possible successor rather than changed by a custom layout mixin.

Use Trinkets Updated 4.1 data-driven client trinket rendering targeted by the supported-lantern tag and gated to legs/lantern, using the actual ItemStack item-model pipeline attached to the canonical body model part with a simple initial hip transform.

Rely on LambDynamicLights 4.12.2's native Trinkets scan and item/block-derived luminance for worn world lighting. Exact source analysis shows allEquipped(false) passes the actual Trinkets ItemStack through ItemLightSourceManager and max-merges it into the same tick/update-driven LivingEntity and chunk-rebuild path used by held equipment, while Iris 1.11.2 and Complementary Unbound r5.8.1 can independently add a per-frame, interpolated-eye handheld shader term from main-hand/off-hand uniforms only; do not add a duplicate LDL source or unsupported hand-light bridge.
Validate survival and creative behavior against Inventory Extended and the accepted Trinkets x Inventory Extended C5 dynamic menu-boundary contract without changing that accepted project.

exclusions: Any modification, normalization, repackaging, redistribution, or tracked copy of originals content; the obsolete reference remains immutable and external to this project.
A source-level port of Simple Belt Lanterns, copied vanilla lantern textures or models, broad legacy compatibility lists, or reliance on its obsolete Radiant Gear dependency.

Replacement or redesign of Trinkets, consumption of legs/belt for lanterns, custom menu-slot insertion, fixed inventory indices, or changes to the accepted Trinkets x Inventory Extended C5 baseline without a demonstrated dependency.

Any Canary 1 custom inventory GUI/layout mixin or belt-absent positioning override; a narrow successor intervention is allowed only if runtime evidence demonstrates that native positioning is inadequate.
Hard coupling to Matcha Flavoured where the normal item-model and resource-pack pipeline provides generic compatibility.

Fake placed blocks, server-side environmental light mutation, fake-hand or inventory-state manipulation, private Iris/shader mixins, a global LDL interpolation change, or making an optional client dynamic-light provider a hard architectural dependency.
Deployment, Minecraft launch, Test Slot occupancy, accepted-baseline changes, instance mutation, or any runtime-validation claim during implementation-only Canary work.

state.milestone: Canary 3 is implemented, clean-built, statically verified, and retained after external Canary 2 feedback reported continued good core wearable behavior, an unwanted palette recolor, and persistently choppier worn light than a held torch. Canary 3 installs the exact user-supplied 16x16 sprite. The expanded source audit proves that held items can combine LDL's tick/update-driven player and chunk-rebuild light with Complementary/Iris's distinct per-frame, interpolated-eye handheld shader term, whereas legs/lantern enters LDL only; because Iris exposes no supported arbitrary equipped-stack hand-light API, no lighting code or speculative bridge was added. An exact A-D shader/LDL runtime matrix remains required. The project remains ACTIVE, not deployed, and formally runtime untested.
